title: what the record states
line: a census son's own field states his relationship to the head, so once the owner accepts him the rule takes the head through it, while the mother and the sister the page relates only by FamilySearch's own groupings stay cards; on the groom's page of a marriage record the bride's parents, whom FamilySearch files as his in-laws, are read as hers, as the record names them: once the groom is accepted the rule takes the bride through what the record states and creates the bride's mother, whom nobody in the tree fits, as her mother, the in-law grouping writing nothing beside it, and the bride's father, given by one name, is nobody to create, a hint and never a card

steps.say: the 1940 census page, focused on the son: his own field says Son, the father's own details say Head, the mother's and the sister's relationship to the head is not on the page
the son accepted by the owner

expect.why: the son's relationship to the head is the census's own statement: the head is taken through it, the tree claiming the link

expect.why: the record names the bride's mother: she is the bride's Mother as stated, not only the groom's Mother-in-law, and nobody in the tree fits her, so the rule creates her
the bride a child of her mother on the record's statement, accepted; the in-law row FamilySearch works out adds no undecided link beside it
the bride's father is stated too, but by one given name: nobody to create, a hint on the page that says why, never a card

steps.say: the rule re-examines: its decisions stand
